verdict:
KILL. No escalation trigger fires: benches concordant at 8/10 and 8/10, no ADVANCE, not held, next print ~2026-11-09 (UNCONFIRMED).

THE COURT-WORTHINESS CASE HAD A DENOMINATOR THAT DOES NOT EXIST IN THE VETTED RECORD. The triage's bull-side dispersion was ~574MW of hard-secured capacity against a ~$2.4B EV, i.e. ~$4.2M per secured MW, a steep discount to where contracted peers mark. Red went to the 10-Q and found the per-site disclosure is 'approximately 60 gross MW' at Panther Creek, 'approximately 63 gross MW' at Scrubgrass, 110 gross MW planned at Sharon and 18 gross MW in Washington. No 350MW. No 574MW. No aggregate pipeline MW anywhere in the filing - while the 8-K markets a '2.2 gigawatt development pipeline'. Blue re-fetched independently and confirmed verbatim, and then did the harder thing: it tested whether this is an apples-to-oranges artifact (current gross energized capacity is a different measure from secured development MW, so divergence could be innocent). It survives the test, because the 10-Q discloses NO development-MW measure at all. The venue choice is the finding.

THE PRIZE TABLE IS THE RULING, AND BLUE'S CORRECTION MATTERS. Red concluded KEEL trades above its fully-funded, fully-leased NPV at ANY rent. Blue showed that is false as stated: red excluded the Washington 18MW and the Hydro-Sherbrooke 96MW conditional transfer from the denominator, and excluded $121M of unencumbered bitcoin from net cash (net debt is ~$136M, not $257M). Corrected, at top-of-market $170/kW-month on 347MW, fully funded and fully leased, NPV is $4.84 per share - about +46% over the tape. So there IS a bull case; it just does not clear the +50% mandate bar anywhere on the vetted record. Clearing +50% needs roughly 360MW at $170 or 590MW at $140 - which means the APPLICATIONS, not the assets. And that +46% best case assumes zero execution slippage against $1.046B of convertible principal (1.375% due 2031 at a ~$6.86 conversion, 1.25% due 2032 at ~$7.41 - both around 2.1-2.2x the tape, so they are debt, not equity) plus a live automatic shelf that permits issuance on any day.

THE 'SOLVENCY REFUTED' LEG WAS HALF THE STACK. The triage credited $458M of converts; the actual principal is $1.046B across two tranches. Cash and restricted cash is $768.9M against $1,025.8M of long-term debt, H1 operating cash use was $117.6M plus $53M capex and $72M prepayments, and roughly $700M of cash funds only about 70-90MW of build at industry shell costs. So the bifurcation the triage claimed - solvency refuted, commercial confirmed - is mislabelled on the first half. What is genuinely confirmed is the commercial half: ZERO signed leases as of the 08-10 print, zero MW energized, first ready-for-service 2027, revenue $30M against $61M a year ago and headed toward zero as the bitcoin stack is sold. The equity is a warrant on interconnect applications.

TAPE CORRECTION AT ADJUDICATION: blue opened by declaring red's tape stale ($3.51, from an earlier pack) versus its own 08-15 18:19Z pack at $3.31, and re-ran all of its arithmetic at $3.31. Verified IBKR daily closes: 08-13 $3.31, 08-14 $3.51. Blue's 'newer' pack was serving the OLDER close and red's $3.51 was correct. Blue's corrected prize table is therefore struck against a price 6% too low, which makes its +46% best case an OVERSTATEMENT - at $3.51 the same $4.84 NPV is +38%, further from the bar. The kill strengthens. This is the same pack-staleness defect as AXTI in this batch, with the same role-reversal.

THE ADVERSE FACTS, ENTERED FAITHFULLY BY BOTH BENCHES: CEO Gagnon made a genuine open-market purchase, 58,888 shares at $3.32-3.33 on 08-13 - token against a $2.17B cap but +4.6% of his own direct holding, which is the honest way to read it. Hiring shows a real wave at Nesquehoning (50 requisitions, 16 in August), though the postings are regional contractors and are not entity-resolved to KEEL's parcel. And blue found the bull-direction omission red leaned past, in the same 8-K red cited: 'three of our priority sites are nearing full permitting with multiple prospective tenants negotiating for each one.' That makes a permit-completion 8-K an earlier and higher-frequency tripwire than the anchor-lease 8-K both benches defaulted to - which is why this is a KILL with tight tripwires rather than a discarded name.

court.record: batch4 8/15; red 8/blue 8 SUSTAINED - outcome CONCORDANT. Blue independently re-read the 10-Q verbatim and confirmed red's denominator FATAL, then corrected red's prize table in the name's favour (red under-counted MW and net cash) - the kill survives with a narrower margin.

reopen_gates: EVENT (earliest clock, and the one both benches missed until blue found it): a permit-completion 8-K on the three priority sites the issuer says are 'nearing full permitting with multiple prospective tenants negotiating for each one'. Higher frequency and earlier than the lease.

EVENT (the one that can actually clear the bar): a signed anchor lease of >= 100MW with an investment-grade tenant at >= $140/kW-month. Re-run the prize table on the day - at that size and rent it can clear +50%.

DATA: any VETTED filing moving pipeline MW into per-site disclosed capacity - i.e. Panther Creek 350MW or Scrubgrass 1.3GW migrating from a utility application into an executed interconnect or ESA in the 10-K/10-Q properties disclosure. This is the denominator that the whole bull case needs and does not have.
DATA (unread by BOTH benches): the 13G filed 2026-07-29 (accession 0002012383-26-002888) - a new >=5% holder that appeared during the spike. Open gap.

BUILD: run plant_thermal on Scrubgrass and carbon_mapper against the waste-coal stacks, and the FEMA NRI join on the PA/WA parcels. All three were UNCHECKABLE at both benches on a name whose entire thesis is physical buildout - this is the largest single coverage hole in the batch and it is checkable next session.
